newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets top ministers over Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets top ministers over Chechnya.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from a heart bypass operation at a country residence, met his defence and interior ministers on Tuesday, the Kremlin press service said.
A spokesman gave no details but Interfax news agency said Yeltsin and the ministers discussed the peace settlement in the breakaway region of Chechnya. The agency did not elaborate.

The communist-dominated opposition in the State Duma lower house of parliament has raised a furore over a deal signed on Saturday by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and the head of the rebel Chechen government, Aslan Maskhadov.
The deal was signed after Yeltsin signed an order withdrawing all Russian troops from Chechnya, including both defence ministry forces and interior ministry ones.
The opposition insists that both Yeltsin's order and the Chernomyrdin-Maskhadov deal are unconstitutional and will lead to Chechnya's secession from the Russian Federation.
The Duma is due to hold an extraordinary session on Friday to discuss the isuue.
The communists have threatened to try and impeach Yeltsin over the order -- a long drawn-out procedure which has little chance of success -- or to call for a no-confidence vote in the government.
